abstract: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, is required to maintain the size and structural stability of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. she mutant embryos develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4 to 5 days post-fertilization, yet the underlying cause has not been identified. Here, we investigated the role of She in recruiting ECM-producing perivascular stromal cells to regulate the structural stability of the DA. She mutants had fewer collagen producing perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein. This correlated with smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, reduced col1a1 transcript and Collagen I pro-peptide levels, and increased DA distensibility. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of a perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell number, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Partial ablation of mural cells alleviated DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to the collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in the vascular endothelium. Together, these findings argue that She functions in the vascular endothelium to recruit and/or maintain perivascular stromal cells, which produce fibrillar collagens required for arterial stability. These results reveal a new mechanism by which signals from the vascular endothelium promote ECM support to maintain arterial vascular stability.
